svg.text: Why the clip on the Broken Ring Illusion is too tight to remove, and the proposed replacement
all mm · arm-local, Z=0 at installed core bottom
A · AS BUILT — arm underside, developed flat
The cantilever is fused to the wrap in three places, so it cannot flex.
Union emits a plain rib — 90° at both ends.
The 37° entry ramp does not exist in the mesh.
Pad sits 1.15 mm inside the R24.5 face,
0.70 mm tall, in a 0.35 mm slot.
Free tip welded to the wrap.
Pad reaches R23.35; the relief that frees it
only reaches R23.15. 0.20 mm of solid weld.
It is a fixed-fixed arch, not a cantilever.
The spring was never the problem.
B · AS BUILT — radial section through the hook
The stem overruns the pocket into solid core and jams.
≈ 0.26 mm³ of hard jam against solid core.
That number IS the jam, not hook retention.
0.05 mm gap under a 0.25 mm skin.
At 0.16 mm layers it prints fused. The release pad is unreachable.
On an FDM part, 0.00 mm of margin is negative.
C · PROPOSED — tapered snap-tab with thumb scallop
Longer tapered beam, engagement above print tolerance, and something to push.
D · PROPOSED — hook profile and dual-mode release
30° in, 45° out. Thumbnail for the deliberate swap, firm pull as override.
The dovetail carries every bit of spin load; the latch only resists axial lift.
A 45° face gives a defined 2.07 N pull-off — far above anything a spinning arm
generates, and a firm deliberate tug by hand. Removal stops being lever-only.
P2S feature tolerance is ±0.10–0.15 mm. At 0.22 nominal, as-printed engagement
lands anywhere from 0.07 to 0.37 mm — 32 % to 168 %. 0.45 mm is ~3× tolerance.
Uniform strain along the span and ~1.6× the deflection for the same peak stress.
That is what pays for the bigger engagement: spring force barely moves, 0.92 → 1.00 N.
Change 0 — wrap clearance 0.12→0.30, core OD relief, lead-in chamfers and validator fixes — is required whatever mechanism wins.
